title: Nicholas Eftimiades on Why the U.S. Doesn’t Get Spying on China Right - The Wire China
gist: A paywall-truncated Q&A intro establishes interviewee Nicholas Eftimiades's credentials as a former 34-year US intelligence-community veteran and author of the first scholarly study of Chinese intelligence operations, before the substantive interview content (on why the US misreads Chinese espionage) is cut off.

insights.claim: Nicholas Eftimiades, a professor of homeland security at Penn State Harrisburg who teaches intelligence with a focus on Chinese espionage, retired after a 34-year US government career spanning the CIA, State Department, Diplomatic Security Service, and Defense Intelligence Agency.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Establishes a credentialed expert source on Chinese intelligence operations worth following for future analysis on China-related espionage risk.
insights.locator: Nicholas Eftimiades is a professor of homeland security

insights.claim: Eftimiades's 1994 book 'Chinese Intelligence Operations' was the first scholarly examination of the structure and methodology of the PRC's intelligence services, and he later updated the research in a follow-up book on Chinese espionage operations and tactics.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Identifies a foundational reference work for anyone assessing PRC intelligence-service structure and tactics.
insights.quote: His 1994 book, Chinese Intelligence Operations, was the first scholarly examination of the structure and methodology of the PRC's intelligence services.
